implementation.name: original-v1-benchmark-coordinated-omission
implementation.scope: Original schematic two-policy timeline; counts of drawn requests only, no measured latency, duration, or percentile.
implementation.question: Why does a closed-loop client record fewer delayed requests?

purpose: Advance one time cursor across the original pause and observe that independent arrivals keep accumulating outstanding requests while the waiting client offers no new load.
storyboard: Establish the shared axis, the shaded pause, and two empty policy rows.
Pause the server before any request is sent.
Send one request from each policy inside the pause.
Independent arrivals continue to four outstanding; the closed-loop client stays blocked at one.
End the pause with every request still outstanding.
Return each policy's first response and record one sample each.
Only then does the closed-loop client send its next request.
Return the last responses; nothing is outstanding.
Compare four recorded pause samples against one, with the waiting-client validity caveat.
guard: TikZ coordinates exactly; no added requests, queue glyph, service bars, millisecond axis, or percentiles. Response order follows the drawing, not a queueing model. The closed-loop result is presented as valid for waiting-client populations, not as wrong in general.
